meta.title: A Day on the Old Town Trail
meta.textType: story: a sequence with linking words

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to the old town. First, they took the town bus from the school gate. The bus was crowded, and the traffic was awful. Lily wrote the time of each stop in her notebook. Leo stood next to the door and held a seat for May. He looked out of the window. "Why is the bus so slow?" he asked. "Many people want to visit the old town today," said Teacher Kim.

Then a guide in a yellow hat met them at the first stop of the trail. "Welcome," she said. "Today we walk for one hour, and we visit four stops." At the first stop, she showed them an old wall and told a story about the history of the town. The wall was gray and tall. The children listened carefully. At the second stop, the children looked at an old well with a red roof. Many tourists took photos there, so Mia waited for her turn. Lily read her notes again.

After that, they came to the small square in the middle of the old town. There was a stage under a big tree, and a dancer stood on it. Classical music came from a speaker, and she began to dance slowly. Her long white dress moved like water. The children sat on the ground and did not say a word. It was quiet in the square. Even the birds were quiet. Mia took one photo, and then she put her camera down.

Next, a young man took the stage with a microphone. He did a rap about the old town, with fast words. Leo clapped with the music and said, "Awesome!" May put her hands over her ears and laughed. "It is awful," she said, "but I like the words about the well." Even the guide smiled. The people in the square clapped. Mia took a new photo.

The final stop of the trail was the market near the river. The children ate cold fruit and sat under a big tree. Everybody was tired. Finally, they walked back to the bus stop, and the bus took them home. This time, the bus was not crowded. That evening, Lily wrote a short post for the blog. She started with the words "First," "Then," "After that," and "Finally."
